EngineContractContractVersionData.title: EngineContractContractVersionData
EngineContractContractVersionData.description: types/engine.d.ts — the frozen PLUR1BUS engine contract. Contract version 1.17.0 (frozen at 1.0.0 on 2026-09-22, owner decision B8; amended seventeen times under the policy below — see the changelog at the end of this header). This file reconciles the four places Phase 0 sketched the same API differently (review-report finding S4). Where ADR-002 and engine-extraction.md §b.2 disagreed, B8 chose: - `Principal.trust: "proved" | "inferred"`   (not `proof: "transport"`) - `TurnOrigin` as a string union plus a separate `AgentContext` (not one `TurnOrigin` object) - `capture()` returns a non-blocking `CaptureHandle` (not `Promise<CaptureResult>`) - `RecallResult.degraded` is a structured object or null (not a boolean) `createEngine` (engine/create-engine.js) implements it from M1b-1 on. It is the shape both the plugin host adapter and the harness are written against, and it is checked by `npm run typecheck`. Amendment policy: "frozen" means 1.0.0 is never edited in place. Any change to an exported member's shape that an existing adapter could observe — a new required property, a removed or renamed member, a narrowed or widened union, a changed parameter or return type — forces a `ContractVersion` bump; only additions no adapter can observe (a comment, a new optional property on a type the engine alone constructs) may land without one. `ContractVersion`, the assertions in `types/engine.conformance.ts` and both adapters move together in a single PR, so the contract, its gate and its two consumers are never in disagreement at any commit. Changelog: 1.1.0 — SecurePathResult.reason gains "acl-tool-unavailable" (Task 5). 1.2.0 — HostServices.workspaceDir becomes async (Task 6). 1.3.0 — HostServices.configPath(), HostServices.routing?, HostServices.pathOverrides? (G1 closure, M1b-1 Task 11). 1.4.0 — Engine surface of createEngine (M1b-1): ContextBlock.chars; RecallResult.timing (replaces timings) and .deferrals; RecallQuery.budget optional; JobRun/JobRegistry/JobSpec per spec 3.3 (outcome gains "abandoned"); CheckpointReason gains "session-end"; Engine.close({ budgetMs }); Engine.channels; HostServices.capabilities?; EngineEventName gains recall.block-clipped/-dropped, recall.completed; createEngine testOptions. 1.4.1 — JobTrigger gains "unknown" (a crash row recovered from a corrupt, unreadable start marker; M1b-1 final review m2). 1.5.0 — MemoryOps types, Engine.memory (E1 Task 2); runCommand deprecated; MemoryState.tombstones number | null (E1-R11); HostCapabilities.memoryArchiveDir? (E1 Task 8). 1.6.0 — AdminOps.share/forget alias Engine.memory (deprecated); ObsidianOps with explicit paths; migrate over a store schema marker; MemoryOps.propose/proposals (D31); MemoryCard.sharedBy/sourceId; MemoryOpError.detail; "memory.proposal" event; EngineStatus.storeSchema (E2). 1.7.0 — EmbeddingService.probe(opts?) → EmbeddingProbeResult (identity, readiness, memoized); serve(address?: IpcAddress | null) → EmbeddingServeResult (real scoped IPC, in-process owner, no claim listener); HostCapabilities.pushCriticalButtons? typed (E3). 1.8.0 — EngineStatus.jobs/models/journal/sharedMemory, degraded derived from model readiness; Engine.models (status, warm); HostCapabilities.journalBacklog?; MemoryOpErrorCode "unsupported"; CaptureResult.reason "duplicate-turn" (E4). 1.9.0 — engine-config.schema.json with readAt/x-tier/x-sensitive and its types (EngineConfigSchema, EngineConfigKey, EngineConfigReadAt); RecallQuery.warmOnly; RecallTiming.totalMs covers queue wait and prelude (E5). 1.10.0 — additive engine-config keys from the 7.18.5–7.18.20 port (runtime.deferPostTurnLlm, diaryFromUserChats, captureChunkingJev, recall.fullTextTopRecords/fullTextMaxChars) and JobName "post-turn-refine"; adapter-only keys stay on the plugin host manifest; no breaking change to existing callers. 1.11.0 — MemoryOps.import (finished-card ingest with deterministic ids) and Engine.stores.adopt (copy-never-move store take-over with a sample cosine probe for legacy stores); MemoryCard.provenance/sourceRef optional; no breaking change to existing callers. 1.12.0 — MemoryOps.rebind / MemoryOps.unbind (manual N:1 channel-identity link; user-scope owner metadata only) and ADOPT_PROBE_MIN_ROWS = min(8, available); UserPrincipal accepts user:v1 and user:v2; MemoryOpErrorCode "identity-already-bound" | "ledger-corrupt" | "lock-lost"; no breaking change to existing callers. 1.13.0 — MemoryOps.unimport (roll back the cards one import run created; archive-first soft delete without a registry tombstone, key freed for re-import); MemoryImportRequest.importRunId optional; MemoryOpErrorCode "lock-busy"; no breaking change to existing callers. 1.14.0 — additive complete vector-space identities, routes and degraded notes. 1.15.0 — HostServices.fetch? (HostFetch: every outbound engine HTTP request goes through it when set); SecretStore becomes resolve(ref, purpose) (lease() kept optional and deprecated; it was never called) for provider `apiKeyRef`; ProviderCredentialConfig, RemoteRerankerConfig and the reranker providers jina | voyage | remote with baseUrl/protocol; no breaking change to existing callers (the engine called no SecretStore member before 1.15.0). Also: MemoryImportRequest without importRunId attributes each card to the run its sourceRef names (`;run=<id>`); MemoryUnimportRequest.importRunId also selects such lines; MemoryUnimportResult.derived.graphEdgesRemoved? / mirrorsArchived? / cleanupErrors? (unimport drops the undone cards' graph edges and archives their Obsidian mirrors). 1.17.0 — AdminOps.reembedding.validate({ id }) (the coordinator's validating → ready_to_switch step: target generation check and semantic recall probe, so a host that owns its switch can finish a migration); a failed validation rejects and leaves the record in validating; no breaking change to existing callers. 1.16.0 — MemoryOps.link(id, req, p, a) (owner decision 2026-10-19: attach an imported duplicate to an existing card as an additional source instead of storing a duplicate; sidecar `_links/`, the card row is never written; idempotent per sourceRef); MemoryCard.links? (show/list); MemoryUnimportResult.links? (unimport of a run unlinks that run's links, the card stays); Engine.capabilities (EngineCapabilities, `memoryLink: true`); no breaking change to existing callers.

warmOnly.description: 1.9.0: run only the read-only heavy path (neo prelude reads, query embedding, read-only store open, vector search, rerank) and answer { blocks: [], degraded: null, timing } on success. Writes no memory data, no store, no file and no persistent embedding-cache row (embeds are memory-only, E5-R26), emits no event, never uses or fills the recall cache, never calls an LLM, runs at background (low, evictable) priority. It warms in-memory caches (the provider's embedding cache, loaded models, the neo worker); a cold local model cache still downloads model files, as any first model load does. A warm recall can also answer blocks [] with degraded "warm-failed" (the warm path failed), "aborted", "timeout", "queue-full" or "pressure" (shed at background priority), or "engine-closed"; a workspace whose policy disables memory answers an empty success.

EngineContractMemoryRecallStatData.description: Every member rejects with MemoryOpError `storage` ("engine is closed") after `Engine.close()`. `list` and `show` read the agent-private pool plus the workspace and user pools the principal can reach. `forget`, `correct` and `share` act on the caller's own agent-private cards. On a shared (workspace/user) copy (D31): `forget` by the sharing agent retracts the copy (archive-first, soft delete; `tombstoneId` is null because the original stays live); `correct` by the sharing agent refreshes it (corrects the original, shares the new version, then retracts the old copy; the result id is the new copy); any other agent answers `denied` and files `propose` instead; `share` of a copy is always `denied`. Proposals never change a memory until the sharer calls `proposals.accept`. A proposal belongs to the shared pool of its copy: `proposals.*` reach it only through a principal that can reach that pool (otherwise `list` omits it and `accept`/`reject` answer `not-found`).

transport.description: API-verified HTTP transport locality; never accepted from browser fields or forwarding headers.

DelegationTargetId.description: Local agent id or an explicitly pinned outbound A2A target. Foreign ids never open local agent stores.

CallerIdentity.description: What the CLI knows about the caller. The core turns it into an engine Principal; a client can never supply trust, origin or incognito.

AuditHealth.description: Experimental cached audit operational metadata for human Owner/Admin with audit.read only. Omitted for all other callers; the public status remains available under its existing policy. At most one read-only metadata scan per 30 seconds, hashing only the latest two complete rows. No record details. state=ok describes whether the observed tail/anchor allows appends, not verification of history. Status never heals or modifies chain evidence.

reason.description: Writer refusal code or audit-unreadable. This is a cached tail/anchor observation, not historical verification.

lastVerifiedAt.description: Last successful explicit audit.verify in epoch ms; persisted across Core/Supervisor restarts. Null until known. Later appends do not change this time.

pendingLines.description: Total number of rows observed in the pending journal (not only the sample in `pending`).

pending.description: Metadata of the newest pending rows, oldest first, at most 50 (AUDIT_PENDING_SAMPLE). `pendingLines` is the total; when it exceeds the length of this array only the newest rows are shown.

models.description: Per-model readiness (E4, spec §6.3); absent before the engine reports it.

journalBacklog.description: Complete lines still in state/journal (live and `.replaying-*` files) as the engine's journal status reports them (E4), or the start replay's kept count when the engine reports none.

deprecationsUsed.description: Deprecated methods/notifications used at least once since start, as `method:<name>`/`notification:<name>`, sorted (ADR-016 §5, S13).

WebSearchStatus.description: Experimental (1.6.0). The state of web.search: which sidecar answers it and what the last attempt showed. Configuration plus the outcome of the last search; no probe runs for this call. `state` is `off` (sidecars.searxng.mode is off), `not-running` (bundled, but the container layer published no address), `misconfigured` (a bad or missing URL), `unknown` (configured, not yet used), `ok`, `unreachable` (connection refused or timed out) or `error` (any other failure, see `lastError`). Never carries a query or a result.

endpoint.description: Origin and path prefix of the configured SearXNG, without credentials.

lastCheckedAt.description: ISO time of the last search attempt.

lastError.description: The web tool failure code of the last attempt, when it failed.

CoreConfigStatus.description: Experimental (1.3.0). The configuration the core runs (B7): `source` is `supervisor` (its `config.watch` snapshot and every `config.changed` since) or `file` (config.json read at start, when no supervisor answered). `revision` is the supervisor's revision of it, null for the file. `restartPending` is true when it differs from the configuration the core started with in a `core`-class key; the supervisor then restarts the core once. Absent before the core has read its configuration.

JournalReplayStatus.description: Experimental (1.3.0). The journal replay a core runs in the background after `ready` (B2): `ready` no longer means the journal is drained. `replayed` counts the lines that left the journal so far; `pendingRemoval` those among them still in the `.replaying-*` file in progress (it is removed when the replay finishes that file, so journal counts include them until then); `kept` is the on-disk count after the last pass and `passes` the number of passes, both set when the replay ends. `aborted` is a stop that left lines unreplayed (they stay for the next start), `failed` a replay that could not read the journal. An empty journal is `done` with zeros at start. Absent before the core is ready.

finishedAt.description: Wall time (ms) the replay ended; null while it runs.

JobsStatus.description: Experimental (1.2.0). Job health as the engine reports it (E4 `EngineStatus.jobs`), flattened on purpose (ruling H3-R6): of the engine's breaker only `open` is kept (as `breakerOpen`; its sweep, session count and limit are dropped), and of each last run only `outcome`, `reason` and `finishedAt` (its runId, trigger, startedAt and attempt are dropped; `jobs.history` has them). Absent before the engine reports it.

running.description: jobs with a run in flight in this process, sorted

breakerOpen.description: the rem/deep LLM-session breaker is open for the current UTC sweep

unreadableLines.description: job ledger lines that could not be parsed

lastRuns.description: latest finished run per job name; jobs that never ran are absent

ModelStatus.description: One model's readiness as the engine reports it (E4). `loading` has `checkedAt: null`; after a completed probe the state stays `ready`/`failed` and a running re-probe shows `warming: true`. `error` only when `failed`. `id`: the embedder's model name or the reranker's provider; null when unknown.

checkedAt.description: epoch ms of the completed probe that set `state`

SharedMemoryStatus.description: Whether explicit shared memory (share/proposals) is available on this platform (E4). "fd-capability": the Linux file-descriptor mode; "verified-path": the path-verified mode the engine uses on macOS and Windows (since engine E4.2); "unavailable": neither works here (`reason` says why).

CrashReason.description: Experimental (1.3.0). The supervisor's crash-reason vocabulary (ADR-012 §10): `ChildStatus.process.reason` of a crashed child and `ChildStatus.lastExit.reason` take these values. `gave-up`: the child exited five times inside the give-up window and is not restarted on its own (its last exit is in `lastExit`); `manifest-invalid` and `api-version-unsupported` are module-only (B12). Documentation: the fields stay plain strings.

ChildStatus.description: One supervised child process as the supervisor sees it. A crashed child's `process.reason` and `lastExit.reason` are $defs/CrashReason values.

adopted.description: true when the supervisor adopted a running child instead of spawning it

nextRestartAt.description: epoch ms of the scheduled restart; null when none is scheduled

kind.description: Experimental (1.3.0). Whether the child is the core, HTTP API or a module; absent from supervisors before 1.3.0.

ModuleState.description: Experimental (1.3.0). A module child's health as the supervisor sees it (module.watch, module.state): its name, its ChildStatus process state, and its pid and instance id while a process runs.

ModuleStatus.description: Experimental (1.3.0). A module process's own status (module.status, module.adopt): its process state, its manifest identity, and its link to the core.

core.description: connected or reconnecting when the manifest needs the core; not-needed otherwise

detail.description: what the module reports about itself (ModuleContext.setDetail)

ModuleListEntry.description: Experimental (1.3.0). One installed module (module.list, B14): its manifest identity (null fields when the manifest is invalid), whether modules.<name>.enabled lets it run, why it cannot start (manifest errors, a needs-cycle, an unresolved need, an unsupported apiVersion), its child while a supervisor runs it (null without a supervisor or before it has a slot), and the last module.status detail the supervisor polled (null when none).

ModuleGraph.description: Experimental (1.3.0). The module dependency graph (module.graph, spec §6.6): the core node first, then every installed module (valid: false with null fields for an invalid manifest); needs-edges and consumes-edges (with the capability); the needs-cycles (members sorted); and what does not resolve (a needs naming a missing or invalid module, a consumes without a provider).

DreamRun.description: One row of the dream run ledger (ADR-009 dream_run). outcome is null while the run is open; every outcome other than completed carries a reason.

claimed.description: True when this run holds the key that makes a rerun over the same corpus and window an idempotent skip.

DreamPlan.description: What dreams.run with dryRun answers: the guard chain evaluated without a ledger row or an engine call.

JournalLine.description: One line of state/journal/<agentId>.jsonl, written by the CLI when the core is unavailable, replayed by the core at start.

ExtAuthAttempt.description: One person's bounded extension sign-in interaction. Credentials, verifiers and callback codes are never returned.

ExtKind.description: Experimental (1.4.0). The kind of an extension: skill, module and channel since X1; mcp-server and bundle added in 1.7.0 (X2).

ExtOverlay.description: Experimental (1.4.0). A derived condition shown instead of the plain state; it never changes the configuration: `needs-setup` (a required secret slot is unfilled), `tampered` (installed files differ from state.json), `revoked` (a revocation matches), `incompatible` (compat no longer holds), `error` (an item in an error state, e.g. a module that gave up, spec 6.2).

ExtTrustTier.description: Experimental (1.4.0). Where an item stands on trust: release (bundled with a release), first-party (signed by a pinned key), unknown-signer (signed by a key the harness does not trust), unsigned, imported (from a skills import) or dev (a local module directory).

ExtAgents.description: Experimental (1.4.0). `"all"` or the agents an item is enabled for.

ExtScript.description: Experimental (1.4.0). One executable file of a package: its path inside the package, its size in bytes, and its first line when it starts with a shebang.

license.description: Since 1.7.0: executable-specific licence when declared; otherwise the package licence applies.

ExtTrust.description: Experimental (1.4.0). The trust verdict of a package: the tier, the signing key id when a signature was present, and the label of the trusted key that verified it.

subject.description: Since 1.7.0: certificate subject when the package carries an X.509 signer.

ExtItem.description: Experimental (1.4.0). One installed extension (ext.list, ext.watch): name, package id (null without a package), kind, version, source (file, bundled, local, ...), trust tier, plain state, derived overlays, whether it is enabled at all, and the agents that effectively have it (skills; "all" for modules and channels).

ExtDetail.description: Experimental (1.4.0). ext.show: the item, its manifest, capabilities and scripts, the trust verdict, a files summary, the extensions that depend on it, and its trash entries.

consentSha256.description: Since 1.7.0: installed bundle consent revision, binding the parent archive and selected member identities, digests, trust and declared rights.

ExtInspection.description: Experimental (1.4.0). ext.inspect (spec 10.2): the id to install with and its expiry (RFC 3339 UTC), the package sha256, the manifest, the trust verdict, the checks (pass, warn or fail), the declared capabilities, the executable files, the requirements, and what an install would replace (with the capability changes).

The cursor survives log rotation. Owner/Admin only (RBAC action logs.query). traceId matches record.trace_id exactly. A push stream needs per-connection notifications the shared RPC server does not have yet; this call is the pull half.

minLevel.description: Not valid with stream audit (E_INVALID_PARAMS reason=level-not-applicable).

component.description: A file role, a record's source.id or source.kind; on the audit stream the first segment of the action.

text.description: Case-insensitive substring, matched against the redacted record (so a search cannot confirm a secret).
