cursor.description: From a previous result of the same call with the same filters (E_INVALID_PARAMS reason=bad-cursor | cursor-mismatch). Stable across appends and log rotation.

audit.verify.description: B5: verifies the hash-chained audit file (logs/audit-chain*.jsonl) and its anchor. Read-only on the log: every line must carry the SHA-256 of the line before it, sequence numbers must be gapless across rotated files, and the anchor (logs/audit-chain.anchor, a separate file) must match the newest line. Owner and Admin only (audit.read). A tampered, deleted or cut-off line is a finding, never an RPC error; findings name a file and a line, never record content. After `plur1bus audit reanchor` the result also lists the era boundaries (reanchors) and the chains set aside (previousChains, each checked only up to its first deviation); neither makes ok false. An unreadable log directory is E_STORAGE. An optional external pin (a sequence and hash recorded elsewhere) is checked under the same lock against the whole chain, rotated files included; pin-missing or pin-mismatch is a finding, and it detects a chain that was rewritten consistently. A successful explicit check also records its time in a private audit-chain.verified.json metadata sidecar; chain evidence is not changed. Failure to persist that time is E_STORAGE.

pin.description: Externally recorded sequence/hash pair; pin-missing or pin-mismatch is a finding.

lastHash.description: SHA-256 of the newest line; pin it outside the host to detect a rewrite of the whole chain.

status.description: behind: the anchor trails the newest line by a write that crashed before the anchor moved (not a finding); ahead: the chain is shorter than the anchor.

findingsTotal.description: All findings; findings carries the first 50.

reanchors.description: Era boundaries in the current chain: each audit.chain.reanchored event, written by `plur1bus audit reanchor` as the first line of a new chain. A note, never a finding; it does not make ok false. Absent from cores older than this field.

at.description: The event's timestamp (ms since the epoch).

suffix.description: The suffix of the set-aside files the event names; null when it names none or not a valid one.

previousChains.description: Chains a reanchor set aside as audit-chain*.pre-reanchor-<ms>, oldest first, each read only up to its first deviation. A deviation there is usually the reason for the reanchor and does not make ok false. Absent from cores older than this field.

announced.description: False when no reanchor event in the current chain names this suffix.

records.description: Lines read before the first deviation.

intact.description: No deviation anywhere in the set and its own anchor matches (or trails by one write).

firstBreak.description: The first deviation, or null when the set was read to its end.

admin.embedding.probe.description: Exercises the embedding provider once (engine EmbeddingService.probe); a successful result is memoized (cached: true) unless refresh is true. A provider failure is ok: false with error, never an RPC error. Bounded by 30 s and by the core's stop (error aborted).

admin.embedding.serve.description: Starts the engine's scoped-embedding IPC server (engine EmbeddingService.serve): address omitted = the engine's platform default, null = stop serving. Idempotent for the address already served. The token itself is never returned, only tokenPath. E_INVALID_PARAMS for a malformed address or a kind the platform does not use, E_CONFLICT when another address is served or the address is in use, E_STORAGE when the listener fails.

admin.embedding.check.description: What the changes of one config.set (plur1bus config set) do to the memory engine's embedding, before anything is written. effect unchanged keeps the running engine's vector space; write is another embedding over a store without data (or under an engine without a usable embedding), which config.set may write and the engine uses from its next start; move is another embedding over a store with data, which only a re-embedding migration reaches: target is what admin.reembed.plan takes, and canSwitch says whether the engine can validate a re-embedded generation (engine contract 1.17.0; without it the migration stops before its switch and the old model stays active). Refuses what the engine could not load, with nothing written: E_INVALID_PARAMS reason=embedding-model-unavailable (an unpinned local model, a block a migration cannot describe, a non-commercial model without its licence acceptance or under the commercial use class), E_CONFLICT reason=embedding-migration-required (a store with data embedded with a non-commercial model would lose its licence acceptance), E_DENIED reason=model-licence-required (a non-commercial memory model without a persisted licence confirmation) and the provider rules of the engine start (E_INVALID_PARAMS reason=engine-provider-config-incomplete, E_DENIED reason=privacy-acknowledgment-required or local-only).

admin.reembed.plan.description: M2 re-embedding migration, step 1 (per installation, not per agent). Builds the compatibility probe verdict for the active store against the target model and, when a migration is needed, the engine's plan: row, table, batch and provider-call counts, byte and free-disk estimates, the pause between batches. Nothing is copied. The confirmation token the engine issues stays in the core and is never returned. `plan` is null when the verdict is compatible or incompatible (with `reasons`). E_CONFLICT reason=migration-active while an earlier migration is unfinished; E_INVALID_PARAMS reason=plan-refused when the engine refuses the plan (e.g. not enough free disk). Every direction is allowed (local or cloud to local or cloud): without provider (or with local-transformers) the target is a pinned local model; any other provider is checked by the same rules as the engine start (model, dimensions and apiKeyEnv required, baseUrl except for openai; E_DENIED reason=privacy-acknowledgment-required without memory.embedding.privacyAck for a non-loopback endpoint, reason=local-only under privacy.localOnly, reason=egress-denied when the egress policy refuses the endpoint). The engine's plan probes a cloud provider with one short text; a cloud plan carries `cloud`: the cards whose text all goes to the provider and the estimated tokens (no cost: the harness has no money dimension).

provider.description: Target embedding provider; default local-transformers (a pinned local model).

baseUrl.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint of a remote target (not for local-transformers); openai may leave it out.

apiKeyEnv.description: Name of the core's environment variable holding the remote target's key; the key itself is never sent.

acknowledgePrivacy.description: The calling person acknowledges now that every card text goes to this remote target (bound to provider and endpoint). Needed when memory.embedding.privacyAck does not already admit the target (e.g. cloud to cloud); the switch writes it as memory.embedding.privacyAck together with the new embedding block.

admin.reembed.run.description: Starts (or continues, after an abort or a halt) the planned migration in the background and returns at once with the checkpoint; follow it with admin.reembed.status. Copies in throttled batches, validates, and (unless switch is false) switches: one config.set that makes the new generation active at the next core start; the old generation is kept. Recall is answered by the old generation until then. With phase ready-to-switch it performs only the switch. E_NOT_FOUND reason=no-migration, E_CONFLICT reason=migration-running|not-runnable, E_NOT_AVAILABLE reason=switch-unavailable.

admin.reembed.status.description: The migration's checkpoint (null when none), the engine's own state for it, whether a run is active in this core, and progress counters.

admin.reembed.abort.description: Stops the migration at the next batch boundary (never mid-batch) and answers with the checkpoint, phase aborted. The copied generation stays and admin.reembed.run continues it. E_NOT_FOUND reason=no-migration, E_CONFLICT reason=not-abortable once it is switched or failed.

supervisor.auth.description: The first call on a supervisor connection; token is the content of run/supervisor.token.

daemon.status.description: The supervisor's own state and one entry per supervised child.

cpu.description: Experimental (1.6.0). The CPU cores every PLUR1BUS process runs on (`supervisor.maxCores`): `detected` cores the system lets the supervisor run on (what a container, cgroup or job allows, not an affinity it inherited; capped by a cgroup CPU quota), `maxCores` as configured (0: no limit), `effective` cores every process may use now, and `state`: `unlimited` (every core), `limited` (bound to `effective` cores), `unsupported` (this OS cannot bind processes to cores) or `failed` (the binding could not be applied; processes keep the binding they had). `reason` explains the last two.

config.description: Experimental (1.3.0). The configuration the supervisor runs (B4): `revision` of the running configuration (null when no valid configuration runs, e.g. config.json was invalid at start) and the last hand edit of config.json it rejected (null once a valid file or a config.set replaced it).

daemon.start.description: Clears a crashed or stopped child's backoff and spawns it.

daemon.stop.description: Replies first, then shuts every child down within budgetMs, removes the supervisor's run files and exits the supervisor.

config.get.description: The running configuration (spec §6.1, B5): the whole value, one key (dotted path) or one tier (key and tier are exclusive). `restartClass` is `live`, `core` or `module:<name>` for a key, else null; `restart` is the same class without the module name (the CLI's `config.get/1` field). `revision` identifies the running configuration (config.set's ifRevision). E_NOT_AVAILABLE reason=config-unavailable when no valid configuration runs.

config.set.description: Validates and applies all changes or none, writes config.json atomically and notifies config.watch subscribers (config.changed, source=set). dryRun only computes the plan. ifRevision refuses a configuration that changed since (E_CONFLICT reason=config-changed, ids.currentRevision). E_CONFIG_INVALID (detail: the joined errors) for a value the schema refuses; E_NOT_AVAILABLE reason=config-unavailable when no valid configuration runs. `restart` is the plan; `restarted` names the units restarted for it. A chain that refuses the audit rows does not block the set; `warnings` then lists audit-chain-unavailable. A failure to write audit.log still refuses it (E_INTERNAL).

revision.description: After an apply the new revision; on a dry run the current one.

estimates.description: Estimated restart time (ms) per unit, null when unknown.

warnings.description: Present only when the set was applied with a caveat. `audit-chain-unavailable`: the configuration is saved, but the audit hash chain refused the audit rows (anchor missing or invalid, integrity mismatch, lock timeout); they are in audit.log with chain=refused and wait in the pending journal until the chain accepts appends again.

config.watch.description: Returns the running configuration and subscribes this connection to config.changed (B3). E_NOT_AVAILABLE reason=config-unavailable when no valid configuration runs.

module.watch.description: Returns every module child's current state and subscribes this connection to module.state (B3).

module.list.description: Every installed module (modules/<name>/module.json) in directory order, with its supervised child (B14).

module.start.description: Clears the module's backoff and starts it (a no-op while it runs); ends a module.stop. E_MODULE_UNKNOWN when no module of that name is installed; E_NOT_AVAILABLE with reason manifest-invalid, api-version-unsupported, scope-agent-unsupported, disabled, needs-unavailable, ext-revoked, ext-tampered or ext-incompatible when it cannot run (the last three: a module installed from a .p1x package is revoked, its installed files changed, or its compat no longer holds).

module.stop.description: Stops the module within budgetMs (default 10000); it stays stopped (reason stopped-by-request) until module.start or a supervisor restart. The persistent switch is modules.<name>.enabled (B13). E_MODULE_UNKNOWN when no module of that name is installed; E_NOT_AVAILABLE with reason manifest-invalid, api-version-unsupported, scope-agent-unsupported, disabled or needs-unavailable when it cannot run.

module.restart.description: Stops the module within budgetMs (default 10000) and starts it again (a requested restart: it never counts toward the give-up budget). E_MODULE_UNKNOWN when no module of that name is installed; E_NOT_AVAILABLE with reason manifest-invalid, api-version-unsupported, scope-agent-unsupported, disabled, needs-unavailable, ext-revoked, ext-tampered or ext-incompatible when it cannot run (the last three: a module installed from a .p1x package is revoked, its installed files changed, or its compat no longer holds).

module.install.description: Installs the module directory at path (B14): copied into modules/<name>.tmp-<pid>, then renamed to modules/<name>. Refused (E_INVALID_PARAMS, nothing copied) with reason not-a-directory, manifest-invalid, symlink, entry-outside or reserved-name. A running module of that name is stopped and started again; a new module starts unless modules.<name>.enabled is false. replaced: a module of that name was installed before.

module.uninstall.description: Stops the module and removes modules/<name>; modules.<name> stays in config.json (B14). E_MODULE_UNKNOWN when no module of that name is installed.

module.auth.description: The first call on a module connection; token is the content of run/module-<name>.token.

module.adopt.description: Called by a supervisor on a running module to adopt it. nonce is the current content of run/supervisor.token; the connection it succeeds on becomes the module's lifeline. E_UNAUTHORIZED reason=adopt-nonce otherwise.

module.shutdown.description: Asks the module to stop within budgetMs; the process removes its run files and exits 0.

ext.list.description: Lists installed extensions (skills, modules, channels), optionally filtered by kind, plain state and the agent that has them. E_STORAGE reason=state-invalid when extensions/state.json cannot be read; an unreadable skills/index.json lists every skill as not enabled.

ext.show.description: One extension in detail. E_NOT_FOUND reason=extension-unknown when nothing of that name is installed. E_STORAGE reason=state-invalid|index-invalid|index-newer (extensions/state.json or skills/index.json cannot be read).

ext.inspect.description: Audits a package file (.p1x, or a skill folder, .zip or .skill normalised to an unsigned package) in a worker process and keeps it for ten minutes; writes nothing under skills/, modules/ or extensions/. E_INVALID_PARAMS reason=package-invalid|signature-invalid|scripts-mismatch|archive-unsafe-entry|archive-unsupported|download-too-large|digest-mismatch|reserved-name|socket-path-too-long; E_CONFLICT reason=name-taken; E_NOT_AVAILABLE reason=incompatible|kind-unsupported; E_DENIED reason=policy-unsigned-disallowed|revoked; E_INTERNAL reason=worker-failed (the worker crashed or overran its 60 s; what it left is removed)|io; E_STORAGE reason=state-invalid|index-invalid|index-newer (extensions/state.json or skills/index.json cannot be read). What a refusal must show is in error.data.ext.

upload.description: Since 1.7.0: one-use ten-minute upload ID, bound to this authenticated person; never a path.

ext.inspection.get.description: Reads an unexpired inspection as the same authenticated human who created it, for the confirmation page. Does not install or consume it. Owner/Admin only; no caller-supplied identity. E_NOT_FOUND reason=inspection-expired for missing, expired or foreign inspection IDs.

ext.install.description: Installs an inspected package, disabled unless enable is given (which needs acknowledge capabilities). Installing the identical package again is a no-op with replaced false. E_NOT_FOUND reason=inspection-expired; E_APPROVAL_REQUIRED reason=acknowledge-unsigned|acknowledge-unknown-signer|acknowledge-downgrade|acknowledge-capabilities; E_CONFLICT reason=busy|name-taken; E_DENIED reason=revoked|policy-unsigned-disallowed; E_INVALID_PARAMS reason=digest-mismatch|package-invalid|agents-not-supported; E_NOT_AVAILABLE reason=kind-unsupported; E_INTERNAL reason=worker-failed (the staging worker crashed or overran its 300 s; its staging and the inspection are removed, inspect again)|io; E_STORAGE reason=state-invalid|index-invalid|index-newer (extensions/state.json or skills/index.json cannot be read); E_LOCKED reason=skills-locked (another writer holds the skills index). What a refusal must show is in error.data.ext.

ext.uninstall.description: Moves an extension into the trash (kept extensions.trashDays days); purge also moves its data. E_NOT_FOUND reason=extension-unknown; E_CONFLICT reason=required-by|busy; E_DENIED reason=bundled (purge of a bundled item). E_LOCKED reason=skills-locked (another writer holds the skills index); E_STORAGE reason=state-invalid|index-invalid|index-newer (extensions/state.json or skills/index.json cannot be read); E_INTERNAL reason=io (a file could not be written; the change was rolled back). trashId is null when nothing went into the trash: a bundled skill is hidden, not moved. What a refusal must show is in error.data.ext.

trashId.description: The trash entry to restore from; null for a bundled skill, which is hidden, not moved.

ext.restore.description: Restores an extension from the trash. E_NOT_FOUND reason=trash-expired; E_CONFLICT reason=name-taken|busy. E_LOCKED reason=skills-locked (another writer holds the skills index); E_STORAGE reason=state-invalid|index-invalid|index-newer (extensions/state.json or skills/index.json cannot be read); E_INTERNAL reason=io (a file could not be written; the change was rolled back).

ext.enable.description: Enables an extension, for the given agents (skills only) or everywhere; dryRun runs every refusal and reports restart and heldBack without writing. E_NOT_FOUND reason=extension-unknown; E_AGENT_UNKNOWN; E_APPROVAL_REQUIRED reason=acknowledge-capabilities; E_NOT_AVAILABLE reason=needs-setup|incompatible|tampered; E_DENIED reason=revoked; E_INVALID_PARAMS reason=agents-not-supported (modules and channels); E_CONFLICT reason=busy. E_LOCKED reason=skills-locked (another writer holds the skills index); E_STORAGE reason=state-invalid|index-invalid|index-newer (extensions/state.json or skills/index.json cannot be read); E_INTERNAL reason=io (a file could not be written; the change was rolled back). What a refusal must show is in error.data.ext.

expectedConsentSha256.description: Since 1.7.0: atomically refuse a changed installed consent revision before activation.

ext.disable.description: Disables an extension, for the given agents (skills only) or everywhere; dryRun runs every refusal and reports restart and heldBack without writing. Disabling a module holds back the enabled modules that need it (listed in heldBack); it is never refused for them. E_NOT_FOUND reason=extension-unknown; E_AGENT_UNKNOWN; E_CONFLICT reason=busy; E_INVALID_PARAMS reason=agents-not-supported (modules and channels). E_LOCKED reason=skills-locked (another writer holds the skills index); E_STORAGE reason=state-invalid|index-invalid|index-newer (extensions/state.json or skills/index.json cannot be read); E_INTERNAL reason=io (a file could not be written; the change was rolled back).

ext.watch.description: Returns every installed extension and subscribes this connection to ext.changed. E_STORAGE reason=state-invalid (extensions/state.json cannot be read; nothing is subscribed).

external.turn.start.description: Start an external turn on an agent session via MCP or A2A.

external.turn.events.description: Read events of an external turn session.

external.turn.get.description: Get session details and optional messages for an external turn session.

external.turn.cancel.description: Cancel an active turn on an external turn session.

decision.status.description: Human-only Owner/Admin aggregate decision health: selected and installed backends, counts, bounded latency window and error rate. Contains no prompts, transcripts, candidate names or model prose. F2 installs only the existing role backend.

decision.test.description: Human-only Owner/Admin bounded decision probe for one agent. Fixed synthetic parity choice, no caller prompt, tools, memory or transcript writes. Uses the production role router with budget, current privacy and auth. Returns aggregate outcome only.

admin.engine.test.description: Human-only Owner/Admin test of the active engine embedder or reranker through engine ports. Fixed small inputs, ten second deadline, no memory or session writes. May contact the configured provider or download local model artifacts under the host policy. Captioner is unsupported: this engine has no captioner role. Returns only safe failure classifications; never provider error messages or credentials.

models.test.description: Human-only Owner/Admin model probe through the configured chat adapter and budget. Fixed prompt, no tools, memory or session writes. Ten second deadline. E_NOT_AVAILABLE reasons model-not-configured, model-test-timeout, model-test-failed. Embedding/reranking probes are not supported.

models.list.description: Lists models in the catalog, provider scan states, new model count, and warnings (D112).

models.scan.description: Scans configured providers for available models, updating the catalog (D112).

models.setOverride.description: Sets or clears metadata overrides for a model, or creates a manual model entry (D112).

models.removeManual.description: Removes a manual model entry from the catalog (D112).

models.acknowledge.description: Acknowledges newly discovered models, clearing the new-models indicator (D112).

budget.status.description: Usage per period (the current local day and month in the configured time zone) and per agent and model, plus every budget limit with its use and state (M2 L8, ADR-010 §4). Counts and ids only; never prompt content. Since 1.11.0, returns the active cacheReadWeight and additive freshInputTokens/countedTokens per period, agent and model. Raw inputTokens still includes cache reads and writes; countedTokens applies the active weight and rounds once per aggregate.

agentId.description: Only this agent's usage, and the global limits plus this agent's own

images.description: Generated images (media units; absent from an older core)

videoSeconds.description: Seconds of generated video, whole seconds rounded up (media units; absent from an older core)

freshInputTokens.description: Fresh input: sum of max(0, inputTokens - cacheReadTokens - cacheWriteTokens) per event. Absent from an older core.

countedTokens.description: Input plus output with cache reads weighted at cacheReadWeight and capped to each event's input. Rounded up once per aggregate. Absent from an older core.

images.description: Generated images (media units; absent from an older core)

videoSeconds.description: Seconds of generated video, whole seconds rounded up (media units; absent from an older core)

freshInputTokens.description: Fresh input: sum of max(0, inputTokens - cacheReadTokens - cacheWriteTokens) per event. Absent from an older core.

countedTokens.description: Input plus output with cache reads weighted at cacheReadWeight and capped to each event's input. Rounded up once per aggregate. Absent from an older core.

freshInputTokens.description: Fresh input: sum of max(0, inputTokens - cacheReadTokens - cacheWriteTokens) per event. Absent from an older core.

countedTokens.description: Input plus output with cache reads weighted at cacheReadWeight and capped to each event's input. Rounded up once per aggregate. Absent from an older core.

cacheReadWeight.description: Active cache-read token weight; absent from a core predating RPC 1.11.0.

egress.status.description: The outgoing-network policy in force (B4): normalised host allowlist, ports, loopback switch, configuration errors (a configuration with errors is deny-all) and counters of per-hop decisions by refusal reason. Read-only; never URLs or addresses.

since.description: RFC 3339: when the counters started (core start)

budget.set.description: Sets, changes or clears a budget limit and/or the time zone budget periods follow (M2 L8). A bound left out stays as it is; null clears it; a limit with no bound left is removed. Bounds are whole numbers in the limit's metric: `tokens` (input + output, output includes reported reasoning tokens), `images` (generated images) or `videoSeconds` (seconds of generated video, rounded up). A media-unit limit gates only media calls that use that unit; there is no money dimension. Since 1.11.0, also accepts cacheReadWeight (0 to 1, rounded to millionths); omitted settings and limits are preserved. Combined updates are atomic.

agentId.description: Required for scope agent, refused for global

cacheReadWeight.description: Cache-read token weight; default 1 counts reads in full. Stored rounded to millionths. Omission preserves the active setting.

limit.description: The limit as stored after the change; null when it was removed. Absent when no limit was supplied.

cacheReadWeight.description: Active cache-read token weight; absent from a core predating RPC 1.11.0.

admin.extensions.setup.get.description: Declared extension secret slots and current availability, never values. Human Owner/Admin only; a missing backend leaves presence unknown. M-A7.

admin.extensions.setup.set.description: Sets one installed extension's declared secret slot as ext:<name>:<slot>. Owner only. The value is write-only and never returned. M-A7.

admin.extensions.runtime.hold.description: Stops an installed MCP registration and holds it while the supervisor changes its package. Direct local Owner connection only; API delegation and module credentials are refused. Returns metadata only. M-A7.

admin.extensions.runtime.release.description: Releases a supervisor transaction hold and reconciles fresh MCP metadata. Direct local Owner connection only; API delegation and module credentials are refused. Returns metadata only. M-A7.

admin.extensions.runtime.status.description: Current MCP runtime holdback metadata for the supervisor. Direct local Owner connection only; API delegation and module credentials are refused. Never returns paths or credentials. M-A7.

admin.extensions.auth.start.description: Explicitly starts a bounded MCP login for this human Owner/Admin and server. Client registration is supplied as a real client ID and literal-loopback redirect URI pair, or by host configuration. Agent discovery never starts login. M-A8.

admin.extensions.auth.status.description: Returns only this initiating human's extension login interaction metadata. Foreign attempts and agent callers are denied. M-A8.

admin.extensions.auth.submit.description: Submits a write-only pasted MCP callback URL to this human's attempt. No callback code, verifier or credential is returned or logged. M-A8.

admin.extensions.auth.cancel.description: Cancels this initiating human's MCP login and invalidates pending callback/device work. No token is returned. M-A8.

secret.status.description: Which secret backend is in use (OS keyring first, then the opt-in encrypted file), why, and how many secrets it holds. Owner only (M2, ADR-005).

secret.list.description: Secret names and metadata, never values. Owner only (M2, ADR-005).

auth.login.start.description: Begins a provider OAuth login (OpenAI: Sign in with ChatGPT, PKCE on a 127.0.0.1 loopback listener). Returns the authorize URL, the loopback port and a login id for `auth.login.await` / `auth.login.cancel`. Human principals only; the Owner's own credentials (D110, ADR-005). The URL is single-use and is never logged.

auth.login.await.description: Waits for a started login to finish (callback, timeout or cancel) and returns the stored credential's metadata. A login whose awaiting connection closes is cancelled. Failures carry `reason`: `state-mismatch`, `access-denied`, `login-timeout`, `login-cancelled`, `port-in-use` and the other closed login codes. Human principals only; Owner only.

auth.login.cancel.description: Cancels a pending login started by the caller; a waiting `auth.login.await` fails with reason `login-cancelled`. Human principals only; Owner only.

auth.credentials.list.description: The caller's saved provider logins: ids, workspace and expiry, never a token or client id. Human principals only; Owner only.

auth.logout.description: Removes a saved provider login and its local token state (provider revocation is attempted). An unknown id is E_NOT_FOUND. Human principals only; Owner only.

agent.pause.description: Human-only lifecycle state. Paused agents admit no new work; archive retains all data. Unarchive preserves the pause flag.

agent.resume.description: Human-only lifecycle state. Paused agents admit no new work; archive retains all data. Unarchive preserves the pause flag.

agent.archive.description: Human-only lifecycle state. Paused agents admit no new work; archive retains all data. Unarchive preserves the pause flag.

agent.unarchive.description: Human-only lifecycle state. Paused agents admit no new work; archive retains all data. Unarchive preserves the pause flag.

agent.export.description: Secret-redacted UTF-8 JSON bundle with an Ed25519 signature of the SHA-256 manifest hash. offerOnly offers an export without reading data; the offer is actor-bound and valid for ten minutes. Agent-private/workspace engine cards plus the authenticated exporter's own user cards only.

agent.delete.description: Archive-first erasure with typed display name and a live export offer. E_NOT_AVAILABLE engine-erasure-unavailable until the pinned engine supplies an erasure API. Never deletes a store directly.

user.list.description: People and role presets, Owner/Admin only.

user.disable.description: Change Core person status; preserve rights, protect the last active Owner and audit.

user.enable.description: Change Core person status; preserve rights, protect the last active Owner and audit.

admin.api.person.resolve.description: API credential only; never exposed to browsers or WebMCP.

admin.api.invite.validate.description: API credential only; never exposed to browsers or WebMCP.

user.role.set.description: Assign a role preset; only an Owner may change ownership. Last Owner cannot be demoted. Audited.

user.invite.create.description: Create a human and a one-time Identity pairing invitation with a fixed role (never Owner). The pairing code is returned here only and lives at most 60 minutes; redeem/confirm through identity.pair.claim/confirm. With params.origin a shareable link (256-bit one-time token, valid ttlMinutes up to 30 days) is returned once as well; only the token hash is stored. Redeem the link through user.invite.redeem.

ttlMinutes.description: Validity of the shareable link in minutes (presets 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d or a custom value up to 30 days). Exclusive with expiresInMinutes; default 60.

origin.description: Web origin (scheme://host[:port], no path) the shareable link is built on. Without it no link is created.

link.description: Shareable one-time link, present only when params.origin was given. Shown exactly once: only its hash is stored.

user.invite.list.description: Invitation metadata without codes or tokens. shareable invitations report their own state (pending, redeemed, revoked, expired) and keep it across restarts.

user.invite.revoke.description: Revoke pending or claimed invitation proof before confirmation. A confirmed link must be unlinked through Identity.

user.invite.redeem.description: Redeems a shareable invitation link's one-time token exactly once and returns the invited person. An unknown, expired, revoked or already used token all answer the same E_INVITE_INVALID without a reason; failed attempts are rate-limited per connection and overall (E_DENIED reason=rate-limited). The token is never logged, audited or echoed.

agent.rights.get.description: List explicitly assigned per-agent rights, Owner/Admin only.

agent.rights.set.description: Assign use/manage; null revokes the explicit right. Role and token scopes still narrow it.

breakglass.request.description: Request an audited read-only window for another person. Affected person receives a durable notice; reason and window bounds come from breakglass configuration (defaults 10-500 trimmed characters, 1-60 minutes).

inbox.list.description: List the authenticated person's own inbox entries, newest first. Dismissed entries are hidden unless includeDismissed. A cursor from a previous page that is not valid fails with E_INBOX_CURSOR.

inbox.count.description: Unread, not dismissed inbox entries per kind (every kind is present) and the number of visible entries, for badges.

inbox.markRead.description: Mark the person's own entries read: `ids` (1-500) or `all: true`, exactly one of them. Ids of other people's entries change nothing. Returns how many entries changed.

inbox.dismiss.description: Dismiss the person's own entries (1-500 ids); they are hidden and count as read. Ids of other people's entries change nothing. Returns how many entries changed.

breakglass.notices.description: Read up to 200 durable break-glass notices affecting the authenticated person. Self-scoped; all human roles. Live grants still require Owner/Admin.

breakglass.list.description: List the authenticated holder's live grants; sweeps expiry and audits it.

breakglass.revoke.description: Revoke a read-only grant; only the holder or an Owner may revoke it.

pairing.qr.description: Read-only formatting of an existing, unexpired pairing link with packages/remote-access QR payload. Does not issue a code, verify an offer tag, pair or store a device. Owner/Admin people only.

auth.status.description: Saved provider logins plus the number of logins in progress. Human principals only; Owner only.

channel.list.description: Every known channel (the config schema's `channels.*` plus any registered with the switchboard): id, whether it is enabled, whether its secrets are all stored (`configured`), and its state and health. `host` is false while the core runs no switchboard, in which case every state is `not-registered`. Owner/Admin, people only (R3).

channel.crypto.description: Experimental owner/admin SAS control for opt-in Matrix memory crypto. Non-persistent; verification is lost after restart. Confirm only after comparing displayed SAS with the peer device. Never returns private keys.

channel.get.description: One channel in detail: effective configuration with every `*Secret` key shown as `{ secret: <name>, present }` (never a value), missing secrets, state, last error, a live health probe when it runs, the key's restart class and how `/link` pairing works on it. Unknown id is E_NOT_FOUND `unknown-channel`. Owner/Admin, people only.

channel.enable.description: Sets `channels.<id>.enabled` to true through the supervisor's `config.set`; the channel's module restarts per the key's restart class. Enabling a channel whose secrets are not stored succeeds and lists them in `missing`. A change that is already in effect writes nothing (`changed: false`). `reason`: `unknown-channel`, `not-configurable`, `config-not-writable` (no supervisor). Owner/Admin, people only.

channel.disable.description: Sets `channels.<id>.enabled` to false through the supervisor's `config.set`; the channel's module restarts (stops) per the key's restart class. Same errors as `channel.enable`. Owner/Admin, people only.

channel.set.description: Sets one key of a channel (`key` is the path under `channels.<id>`, e.g. `allowlist` or `imap.host`). Give exactly one of `value` (a JSON value) or `text` (the raw text, interpreted by the key's schema type so ids with leading zeros or 25 digits survive). The result is validated against the config schema before anything is written. A `*Secret` key takes a secret NAME: a value that looks like a credential is refused with `reason: secret-value` and is never echoed or stored. `reason`: `invalid-key`, `unknown-key`, `invalid-value` (`detail` names the schema complaint), `value-required`, `secret-value`, `unknown-channel`, `not-configurable`, `config-not-writable`. Owner/Admin, people only.

channel.test.description: Health check of one channel (a live probe when it runs). With `sendOwner: true` it also sends one fixed test text to the caller's own linked identity on that channel (never to a recipient the caller names); that needs the write action. `reason`: `channel-not-running`, `owner-not-linked`, `send-failed`. Owner/Admin, people only.

channel.status.description: All channels, compact: id, enabled, state, health and the last error. Owner/Admin, people only.

media.search.description: Searches the media index (image, video, audio) with text or by a medium it already knows: give exactly one of `text` and `likeMediaId`. A text query is embedded by the TEXT encoder of the MEDIA model (vectors of different spaces are never compared). `kinds` narrows the result, `limit` defaults to 20. With `fuseCaptions` the ranks are fused with the caption hits of the text index (reciprocal rank fusion over ranks, never over vectors). Results are filtered to the media the caller may read; an agent sees its own scope. Reasons: `text-or-like-required` / `text-and-like-exclusive` (E_INVALID_PARAMS). E_MEDIA_* codes: the media index refused or cannot run (capability, licence, “Only local models”, availability, dimension, unsupported kind). Every principal with read access; agents within their own scope.

media.index.status.description: State of the media index: whether it is enabled, provider, model, dimension and fingerprint, counts per state and the backfill progress. Every principal with read access (agents included).

media.index.pause.description: Pauses the background backfill of the media index (pausedReason `user`). Idempotent. Returns the new status. Owner/Admin, people only.

media.index.resume.description: Resumes a paused backfill of the media index. Idempotent. Returns the new status. Owner/Admin, people only.

media.index.reindex.description: Starts a full re-index of the media index in the background. `confirm` must be true (E_INVALID_PARAMS reason=confirmation-required otherwise). Returns the new status. Owner/Admin, people only.

media.caption.set.description: Sets the caption of a medium (source `user`); the caption is a memory entry of the text index and is re-embedded. E_NOT_FOUND when the medium is unknown or the caller may not see it, E_DENIED when the caller may not edit it. People who may edit the medium; agents never.

secret.describe.description: Owner and human only. Changes a secret description without supplying or exposing its value. Empty description clears it. Rejects any contiguous secret fragment of at least eight characters. Backend validates under its serialization; credential bytes and existing leases are unchanged. Audited before mutation.

secret.grants.list.description: Owner and human only. Read-only effective agent lease grants and separately labelled config references. Agent leases are currently disabled, so grants is empty; a configuration reference never grants authority. No secret values or lease handles.

secret.set.description: Creates or replaces a secret, with an optional description; leases on the old value are revoked. The value is write-only: the result carries metadata only. A value of fewer than 8 characters is accepted, but the log redactor does not mask values that short, so the result then carries a `warning`. Owner only; every call is audited (M2, ADR-005).

description.description: What the secret is for (one line of plain text, at most 200 characters, never the value); the agent's `secret_names` tool shows it. Absent: a replacement keeps the stored description. Empty: removes it.

secret.get.description: A secret's metadata; with `reveal: true` also its value, the only RPC that returns one. Owner only; the call is audited before the value is released (M2, ADR-005).

secret.delete.description: Deletes a secret from every available backend and revokes its leases. Owner only; audited (M2, ADR-005).

identity.list.description: Experimental (1.5.0, M3). Lists humans with their active linked channel identities (revoked ones with includeRevoked) and the pairings that still wait. Owner only: the CLI caller. Never contains a pairing code.

identity.human.create.description: Experimental (1.5.0, M3). Creates a human principal (an opaque UUIDv7 id). Owner only. Audited.

identity.link.description: Experimental (1.5.0, M3). The owner links a channel identity to a human by hand (proof owner_manual); never inferred. E_CONFLICT when the identity is already linked (N:1: an identity belongs to at most one human). Owner only. Audited.

identity.pair.start.description: Experimental (1.5.0, M3). Mints a one-time pairing code for a human on a channel: 8 characters, valid 10 minutes, single use, at most 3 pending per human and channel. The code is in this result only, once; it is stored as a salted hash and never logged. Owner only. Audited.

identity.pair.claim.description: Experimental (1.5.0, M3). A channel adapter relays a code a person sent from a channel identity. A match consumes the code and parks the claim for the owner (links nothing). A wrong, expired, reused or wrong-channel code is E_DENIED reason invalid-code; failures are rate limited per identity and overall (E_DENIED reason rate-limited, detail retryAfterMs=N). E_CONFLICT when the identity is already linked.

identity.pair.confirm.description: Experimental (1.5.0, M3). The owner approves or declines a claimed pairing. Approving links the identity (proof pairing_code). Owner only. Audited. E_DENIED reason expired when the claim was not confirmed in time; E_CONFLICT when the pairing is not waiting or the identity was linked meanwhile.

identity.unlink.description: Experimental (1.5.0, M3). Revokes a link at once: the identity stops resolving to the human and leaves the union of linked principals. The record stays for the audit trail. Rows written under its v1 principal become unreadable to the human until it is linked again (ADR-007). Owner only. Audited.

session.model.get.description: Read the owned session model profile, effective default, revision and reasoning choice. Incognito stays in RAM. Same transcript authorization as session.get.

session.model.set.description: Preview a model-profile switch and its cache/cost warning; applies only with confirmed=true and the preview revision. Own idle direct sessions only. Per-model stable prefixes are retained. reasoning (since the per-chat reasoning choice) sets the chat's reasoning level with the profile; absent keeps the stored choice.

session.create.description: Opens a session for the caller (the owner is derived from the caller identity). Only direct and channel sessions are created here; card/project/acp sessions belong to their modules. A channel session needs chatKey and, per D21, at most one is active per chat: a second create is E_CONFLICT unless replaceActive archives the first (/new).

session.list.description: Authenticated metadata listing: Owner/Admin/Operator/Viewer may filter all owners and agents; Member sees only their own sessions. No transcripts; searching another owner's transcript is denied. Omitting owner and allOwners preserves own-session listing; allOwners=true selects all metadata.

session.get.description: One session of the caller's (archived ones included), with the id of its running turn (if any) and, when messages is given, the last that many messages. Another owner's session is E_NOT_FOUND. Foreign transcripts require a live audited Break-Glass grant; the authenticated principal determines ownership.

includeHidden.description: Also return the tool outputs the context view hides (hiddenToolOutputs). Off by default; it adds no rights, the same transcript gate applies.

hiddenToolOutputs.description: Present only with includeHidden: the tool outputs hidden from the context view, with their originals from the event log.

compaction.description: Context-only hidden tool refs and applied summary original ranges. Full transcript is unchanged.

session.resume.description: Get plus the transcript (the last `limit` messages, default 100) and the last event seq, so a client can continue from the next one. An archived session is E_CONFLICT. Foreign transcripts require a live audited Break-Glass grant; the authenticated principal determines ownership.

session.archive.description: Archives a session (archive-first deletion: nothing is removed; there is no delete over RPC). Idempotent. A session with a running turn is E_CONFLICT.

session.submit.description: Submits one user message and starts a turn. Returns at once with state running (events follow as session.event notifications and through session.events), or, with wait, after the turn ended with its state, reply and error. One running turn per session (else E_CONFLICT turn-in-progress); no configured provider is E_NOT_AVAILABLE reason no-provider. Recall and capture happen once per turn inside the core; memory mode is the session's, never a parameter.

session.events.description: The session's persisted events after afterSeq (default 0), oldest first: the same stream session.event delivers, for replay and catch-up. running tells whether a turn is still producing events. Foreign transcripts require a live audited Break-Glass grant; the authenticated principal determines ownership.

session.cancel.description: Cancels the session's running turn: it ends failed with error cancelled (what was already streamed stays stored; nothing is captured). Idempotent: with no running turn nothing happens and cancelled is false.

grant.list.description: D109 §4: the grants in the approval store, newest first, optionally filtered. Owner/Admin only (RBAC action grant.read); refused for every agent principal (RBAC humanOnly), and never a tool in an agent catalogue, the D103 index, WebMCP (the admin.* rule, B15) or the harness MCP server. limit defaults to 100; cursor comes from a previous result with the same filters (E_INVALID_PARAMS reason=bad-cursor). A broken approval chain lists the affected grants as suspended; it is not an error here.

grant.get.description: D109 §4: one grant of the calling person. Owner/Admin only (RBAC action grant.read); refused for every agent principal. E_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id or another person's grant. A broken approval chain returns the grant as suspended.

grant.create.description: D109 §4: a person gives an agent a standing permission (scope task, session or always; once grants are made only by approval.decide). The grant belongs to the calling person; the surface level is derived by the core from the connection and never accepted as a parameter. Owner/Admin only (RBAC action grant.write), refused for every agent principal. Audited. E_DENIED reason=policy-never (the capability is never grantable: credential.entry, harness.admin, policy.bypass ...) | surface-untrusted (the connection's surface is below what the capability and scope need). E_INVALID_PARAMS reason=ceiling-exceeded (the scope is wider than the capability allows) | invalid-grant | duplicate-id. E_AGENT_UNKNOWN.

grant.revoke.description: D109 §4: revokes a grant. Immediate: pending requests it covered return to asking and the next call of a running task is re-decided. Idempotent: revoking a revoked grant returns it unchanged. Owner/Admin only (RBAC action grant.write), refused for every agent principal. Audited. E_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id.

approval.list.description: D109 §5: approval requests, newest first. The pending queue is status=pending (there is no separate approval.pending method). Owner/Admin/Operator (RBAC action approval.read); refused for every agent principal. limit defaults to 100; cursor as in grant.list. Records never carry the nonce.

approval.get.description: D109 §5: one approval request with everything a person needs to decide it. Owner/Admin/Operator (RBAC action approval.read); refused for every agent principal. E_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id.

approval.decide.description: D109 §5: a person approves or denies a pending request; the first valid answer wins and the other surfaces close. approve may pick one of the request's grantOptions as `scope`; the narrowest is the default. The surface level is derived by the core from the connection and checked against the request's requiredSurface; nothing is ever approved by a timeout or a surface default. nonce is the request's one-time nonce, required where the answer is relayed by a channel. Owner/Admin only (RBAC action approval.decide), refused for every agent principal. Audited. E_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id. E_DENIED reason=surface-untrusted (the connection's surface is below requiredSurface) | approval-expired | approval-used (already decided or consumed) | approval-mismatch (nonce or binding differs). OS attestation (issue #192): a request that needs T2 and is decided on an unattested local connection (T1) can be lifted to T2 by ONE confirmation of the operating system (Touch ID, Windows Hello, UAC consent, polkit), valid for this approval only (bound to the request, scope and agent, used once, at most 60 s). Without `attest` such a call is E_APPROVAL_REQUIRED reason=attestation-required (detail = the method that will be asked, e.g. touch-id) and nothing is shown; with `attest: true` the core opens the OS dialog itself and decides at T2 when the person confirms. E_DENIED reason=attestation-failed (detail = cancelled | timeout | failed | replay | mismatch; the request stays pending); E_NOT_AVAILABLE reason=attestation-unavailable (no helper, container mode, no graphical session: the T1 limits stand); E_CONFLICT reason=attestation-in-progress (another decision of the same request is waiting for its dialog). Never for a nonce-relayed decision, an agent principal or a request that needs T3.

attest.description: Consent to the OS confirmation dialog this decision may need (see the method description). Default false.

grant.description: The grant created by an approval whose scope is wider than once; null otherwise.

approval.cancel.description: D109 §5: withdraws a pending request (status cancelled); the waiting call receives a typed denial with a userAction sentence. Owner/Admin only (RBAC action approval.decide), refused for every agent principal. Audited. E_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id; E_CONFLICT when the request is no longer pending.

approval.verify.description: D109 §6/§9.7: verifies the HMAC-SHA256 chain of the approval store and additive Ed25519 signatures on decisions (the `1staid check approvals.integrity` check, on demand). Read-only. A broken chain is a finding (ok false, brokenAt, reason), never an RPC error; a broken chain suspends every grant after the break. Unsigned legacy entries remain valid. Owner/Admin/Operator (RBAC action approval.read); refused for every agent principal.

head.description: The newest entry; null for an empty chain. Pin it outside the host to detect a rewrite of the whole chain.

brokenAt.description: First seq at which the chain does not hold. Present only when ok is false.

reason.description: Present only when ok is false.

signatures.description: Additive Ed25519 status. Unsigned legacy entries remain valid.

approval.audit.description: D109 §9.10: approval-related HMAC-chain entries of the calling person, newest first, redacted (no nonce, no raw payload). Owner/Admin/Operator (RBAC action approval.read); refused for every agent principal. limit defaults to 100. This is a view of the existing approval chain, not a second audit log.

BudgetLimit.description: Experimental (1.5.0). A budget limit. Bounds count the metric: input + output tokens (output includes reported reasoning tokens), generated images, or seconds of generated video.

BudgetLimitState.description: Experimental (1.5.0). A budget limit with its use in the current period and where that stands.

IdentityHandle.description: Experimental (1.5.0). A channel handle. displayName is a label for people and is never matched on.

IdentityHuman.description: Experimental (1.5.0). A human principal: an opaque UUIDv7 id, never reused.

IdentityLink.description: Experimental (1.5.0). A channel identity linked to a human, with how it was proved and whether it was revoked. v1Principal is the engine's v1 principal of the handle (the read side of the union recall).

IdentityHumanEntry.description: Experimental (1.5.0). A human with its linked identities.

LogStream.description: diagnostic: logs/<role>.log (+ rotated copies); audit: logs/audit.log. payload.log is never served.

ts.description: Normalised RFC 3339 UTC, millisecond precision (a legacy `at` field is normalised the same way).

component.description: The file's role (core, supervisor, ...; audit for the audit stream).

record.description: The line as written, after reader-side redaction (D111 section 4): secret-looking keys and credential shapes are replaced by [REDACTED:<rule>].

nextCursor.description: Opaque; send it back with the same filters. logs.query: null when nothing more lies in that direction. logs.tail: always set after the first call.

corrupt.description: Lines looked at that were not a valid record (not JSON, no timestamp, bad level, over-long). Counted, never fatal; an unterminated last line is not counted, it is the writer's line in flight.

truncated.description: The per-call scan budget ran out before the page was full; nextCursor continues from the last line looked at.

IdentityPairing.description: Experimental (1.5.0). A pairing that still waits (a pending code, or a claim waiting for the owner). Never carries the code.

ChatReasoningChoice.description: A chat's reasoning / thinking intensity on the harness scale (cheapest first), or default: send nothing and let the provider decide. Each attempt maps it onto the model's own levels (nearest supported) and wire parameter.

ChatModelOption.description: One configured model profile a chat may pick, described by its primary model. A locked profile stays listed with selectable false and the reason (local-only: “Only local models” is on and a candidate is not local; unavailable: the catalog no longer lists the model).

reasoning.description: What the primary model offers. kind none: no setting (the model reasons on its own or not at all). source: the provider's own model list (api), the curated table (table) or nothing known (unknown).

SessionRecord.description: One session (M1b-2c, D92 §2.1). kind, agentId, owner scope and chatKey are immutable (I1). The overview adds owner, model/provider and usage metadata. Transcript access stays owner-scoped or explicitly audited through break-glass.

SessionEvent.description: One event of a session's ordered stream. seq is per session, starts at 1 and has no gaps; data's shape depends on type.

RestartPlan.description: Experimental (1.3.0). A restart plan (ADR-013 §3): the changed live keys, whether the core restarts, and the modules that restart.

IpcAddress.description: An IPC endpoint (engine IpcAddress): a Linux abstract socket name, an absolute unix-socket path or a Windows named pipe.

cloud.description: Present for a cloud or self-hosted target: every card text goes to this provider. estimatedTokens is an upper bound from the source size without its vectors (the budget counts tokens; there is no cost estimate).

ReembedCheckpoint.description: The migration's Harness checkpoint without the engine's confirmation token. `aborted` is stopped and resumable (by request or after an engine error: see error); `validating` with error engine-validate-unavailable waits for an engine that can validate (one before contract 1.17.0); `switched` and `failed` are final.

remote.description: A cloud or self-hosted target: the name of the environment variable holding its key (never the key), the endpoint as configured, and the per-card token estimate the call budget reserves before each batch. A budget refusal pauses the run (phase aborted, error budget-exceeded).

score.description: present on a topic listing, absent on show

sharedBy.description: workspace/user copies only: the sharing agent, possibly another host's (never constrained to AgentId)

sourceId.description: workspace/user copies only: the sharer's original card

resultId.description: accepted: the id of the refreshed shared copy

ModelEntry.description: One model in the harness catalog (D112).

toolUse.description: D97 host-eval status; missing, stale, fake or incomplete evidence is unknown.

new.description: true until the person acknowledges the model via models.acknowledge

locked.description: Present when the model may not be used now: local-only means privacy.localOnly is on and the model's provider endpoint is not loopback or listed in privacy.localEndpoints. Locked models are listed, not hidden.

ModelProviderState.description: Scan state of one model provider (D112).

ModelScanWarning.description: Warning from a model scan or catalog state (D112).

ChannelRestart.description: Experimental (1.5.0). The restart plan of a config change: live keys, whether the core restarts and which modules restart.

ChannelSummary.description: Experimental (1.5.0). One channel in a listing. `configured` is true when the channel has a configuration here and every secret it references is stored.

profile.description: Effective restrictive behaviour, keyed by section and field.

ChannelDetail.description: Experimental (1.5.0). One channel: summary plus effective configuration (secrets as names), missing secrets, status, probe and pairing help. Never a secret value.

behaviour.description: ADR-003 effective direct/group policy with per-field source paths and the channel-kind layer editable by owner/admin. Null if no unambiguous default agent exists.

MediaSearchHit.description: Experimental (1.5.0). One hit of `media.search`; `segment` locates the match inside a video or audio, `caption` is the caption text when the caller may read it, `thumbnailUrl` is a URL the web UI can load.

MediaIndexStatus.description: Experimental (1.5.0). The state of the media index and its backfill.

AuthCredential.description: Experimental (1.5.0). A saved provider login (D110): opaque id, owner, workspace, expiry. Never a token, refresh token or issued client id.

SecretMeta.description: Experimental (1.5.0). A secret's name, timestamps and optional description; never its value (M2, ADR-005).

updatedBy.description: Person ID of the last writer, when known; never a secret value.

description.description: What the secret is for, as the owner wrote it; absent when none was given. Never a secret value.

SecretSetOutcome.description: Experimental (1.5.0). What `secret.set` returns: the same fields as SecretMeta, plus a `warning` when the value is too short for the log redactor to mask. Never the value.

updatedBy.description: Person ID of the last writer, when known; never a secret value.

description.description: What the secret is for, as the owner wrote it; absent when none was given. Never a secret value.

warning.description: Present when the stored value has fewer characters than the redactor masks: the value was stored, but it could appear unmasked in a log line.

minMaskedChars.description: The shortest value the log redactor masks (8).

message.description: English text for clients without a message catalogue; the code is the stable part.

SecretStatus.description: Experimental (1.5.0). The secret store's state: `backend` is where values go now (`none` when neither the OS keyring nor the enabled encrypted file can serve), `degraded` is true whenever it is not the keyring (M2, ADR-005).

secrets.description: Persisted metadata only. Unknown legacy timestamps and writer are omitted.

ApprovalId.description: Experimental (1.5.0, D109). The store id of an approval request (apr_<hex>).

GrantId.description: Experimental (1.5.0, D109). The store id of a grant (grt_<hex>).

ApprovalStatus.description: Experimental (1.5.0, D109 §5/§6). pending: waiting for a person; approved/denied: decided; used: an approved once-decision was consumed by its call; expired: nobody answered within 24 h (= denied, E_DENIED reason=approval-expired); cancelled: withdrawn through approval.cancel.

GrantState.description: Experimental (1.5.0, D109 §4/§6). suspended: set aside by a broken approval chain (fail closed) or the §8 taint rule; ends by time (expiresAt, scope bound) are derived by the reader.

GrantScopeName.description: Experimental (1.5.0, D109 §4). How long a grant lasts: one call (action hash), the task, the session, or until revoked (auto-expires after 90 days unused).

SurfaceTrustLevel.description: Experimental (1.5.0, D109 §5). T0 nothing, T1 inbound ACP editor (low only), T2 web session without step-up or a private linked channel chat, T3 desktop app, CLI on a TTY of the owning OS user, web with step-up. Derived by the core from the connection, never supplied by a client.

ApprovalSubject.description: Experimental (1.5.0, D109 §6). Who the call runs for: the agent (or helper, peer, client) and its id.

GrantMatch.description: Experimental (1.5.0, D109 §3/§4). action: one call (the action hash); capability: the whole capability inside roots; path: a canonical path, read or write (write implies read), recursive or the direct children only.

GrantRecord.description: Experimental (1.5.0, D109 §4/§6). A grant as the store holds it. Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC.

surface.description: The surface level the grant was given on.

attestedVia.description: Present when an OS confirmation (attested:touch-id, attested:windows-hello, attested:polkit ...) lifted the approval that created this grant to T2.

ApprovalRecord.description: Experimental (1.5.0, D109 §5/§6). An approval request as the store holds it. The one-time nonce is never part of it. Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC.

osConfirmation.description: Connection-relative OS confirmation state. A status is informational; approval still verifies a fresh, action-bound attestation.

principal.description: The person on whose behalf the call runs, and the only one who may decide it.

grantOptions.description: Narrowest first; the first entry is the pre-selected one.

targets.description: The exact, redacted targets (paths, URLs, package list) the call touches.

summary.description: The exact, redacted command line or diff summary; shown before anything the model wrote.

agentReason.description: The model's own `why`. Unverified; clients label it so.

diff.description: A redacted unified-diff or patch the model supplied with the request. Unverified; clients label it so.

InboxKind.description: Closed set of inbox entry kinds; also the only metric label of the inbox.

InboxEntry.description: Metadata only: the client translates `titleKey` and fills it with `params`; `ref` names the route and object to open. No secrets, no content.

egress.changed.description: Engine policy cache invalidation; emitted when the core's egress policy changes.

import.progress.description: Bounded maintenance counters only; no source paths, content or secret values.

devices.trust.next.description: Staged next certificate trust over authenticated current-trust connections; addressed only to paired device owners.

api.account.changed.description: Core person authority changed; connection-targeted to authenticated API service listeners only.

voice.realtime.state.description: Private Voice V3 event; delivered only to authenticated connections in the originating audience.

voice.realtime.transcript.description: Private Voice V3 event; delivered only to authenticated connections in the originating audience.

voice.download.progress.description: Private Voice V3 event; delivered only to authenticated connections in the originating audience.

inbox.changed.description: The authenticated person's inbox changed; refresh with inbox.count / inbox.list. Carries no entry data. Opt-in and fail closed: withheld unless every subscriber that named it is that person.

project.card.changed.description: Committed project board invalidation delivered only to current authorized readers. Refresh the project board, including reordered siblings.

project.column.changed.description: Committed project board invalidation delivered only to current authorized readers. Refresh the project board, including reordered siblings.

x-deprecated.replacement: harness event notifications: recall.completed, recall.degraded, recall.block-clipped, recall.block-dropped, job.run, memory.proposal (ADR-016 §6)

engine.event.description: Every engine event forwarded verbatim: name is the EngineEventName, payload as emitted, agentId when the payload carries one. Delivered only to subscriptions that name engine.event in names (opt-in).

recall.completed.description: One per recall attempt: total wall time and whether it degraded.

recall.degraded.description: A recall exited degraded (timeout, abort, pressure, store error, ...).

recall.block-clipped.description: The inject-budget join clipped a context block from `from` to `to` characters.

recall.block-dropped.description: The inject-budget join dropped a context block (`to` is 0).

job.run.description: One per finished job run (the ledger row without counts, cost and keys).

memory.proposal.description: A change proposal against a shared copy was filed or resolved (D31). agentId is the sharer; delivered to subscriptions filtered to the sharer or the proposer. Agent ids are plain strings: a copy may come from another host's agent.

dream.completed.description: Declared by the engine contract but not emitted by the pinned engine; no payload fields beyond agentId (G11).

acl.denied.description: Declared by the engine contract but not emitted by the pinned engine; no payload fields beyond agentId (G11).

embedding.identity.changed.description: Declared by the engine contract but not emitted by the pinned engine; no payload fields beyond agentId (G11).

config.changed.description: The running configuration changed (B3), sent on connections that called config.watch. `config` is the full new configuration; `source` is `set` (config.set) or `file` (a hand edit of config.json the watcher applied). `previousRevision` is null when no valid configuration ran before.

module.state.description: A module child's health changed (spawned, ready, degraded, orphaned, stopping, stopped or crashed), sent on connections that called module.watch.

ext.changed.description: An extension's kind, state, version or overlays changed (install, uninstall, restore, enable, disable, integrity), sent on connections that called ext.watch. `state` is installed or enabled, or removed once the extension was uninstalled (then version is the removed version and overlays is empty).

chat.models.changed.description: Payload-free invalidation of chat model options after accepted privacy policy changes. Clients reread their authorized chat.model.get; no configuration, agent ID or credential is broadcast.

models.changed.description: Emitted when a scan alters available models in the catalog (D112).

session.event.description: One event of a session's stream (turn.started, delta, tool.call, tool.result, turn.completed, turn.failed), sent as it is persisted. Delivered only to subscriptions that name session.event in names (opt-in); an agentId filter on the subscription applies. The same events are replayable with session.events.

approval.requested.description: D109 §5: a new approval request is pending. Opt-in (a subscription must name approval.requested in names) and delivered only to subscriptions of person principals with approval.read; never to an agent. The record carries no nonce.

approval.resolved.description: D109 §5: a request left pending (approved, denied, expired or cancelled). The first valid answer closes it on every surface. Opt-in (a subscription must name approval.resolved in names) and delivered only to subscriptions of person principals with approval.read; never to an agent.

approval.parked.description: D109 §5: the foreground wait ended and the request stays open until TTL. Opt-in (a subscription must name approval.parked in names) and delivered only to subscriptions of person principals with approval.read; never to an agent. The record carries no nonce.

grant.changed.description: D109 §4: a grant was created, used, revoked, expired or suspended. Opt-in (a subscription must name grant.changed in names) and delivered only to subscriptions of person principals with grant.read; never to an agent.
